Preserve the author's meaning, context, theological position, assertions, negation, modality, uncertainty, attribution, and intention. Use natural target-language grammar and idiom. Fidelity means preserving the printed meaning, not retaining English wording. Do not substitute another Bible version or copy, retain, or restore English quoted prose as a fidelity workaround. Translate book names into conventional target-language forms, preserving the printed reference identity, exact chapter/verse numbers, ranges and the number and placement of references. Preserve proper names, dates, measurements, credits, and attribution; transliterate only where normal in the target script. Proper names, established titles of cited works, and identifiers may remain unchanged where appropriate to the target language; this does not exempt quoted prose or translatable article metadata. When the babies are out of diapers...
When I can get a full night of sleep...
When the children are old enough to help...
When homeschooling is finished...
When the teenagers are grown up...
When the children are married...
If I had been taught to keep house...
If I only had a baby...
If I had a husband who...
If my children would...
If our finances weren’t so tight...

Have you ever heard these cries, or thought them yourself? So many, many times through the years I have found myself saying many of these things. In the middle of the baby years, with a baby in my arms, toddlers hanging on my skirts and a preschooler, I wished for someone to help with the chores. Later, there were plenty of helpers, but more work and home-schooling to accomplish and I was sure that this was the most difficult time of my life. Still later, when my last babies were tiny, and we were sitting up to chat with young people facing life-changing decisions, I was saying other “ifs.” So soon, the babies stopped coming and I wasn’t nursing any more but my nights were interrupted because of changing hormones. The temptation to be discontented was still there. Some ladies never have problems sleeping even with hormone changes....

As I was thinking about the last thirty years, I realized that one of the things that had sapped too much of my vitality was discontentment and murmuring. I remembered the joyful, singing girl that became a mother and somewhere, some of the song was lost. Where did it go when I did not have it? Why was it too often gone? I see so many, many tired, frustrated mothers who do not have the joy of Jesus on their faces. What is the answer? What have I learned over the years?

When we were married, I was joyful, and full of song. In fact, singing characterized my life. I had learned through some very, very difficult experiences of being alone, that Jesus was all I needed. When I met with Him and walked with Him my heart overflowed with song. So when I met and married my husband, my cup was really full and overflowing. Now I had a person to walk with me and to share with. I was very happy.

The babies began to come and I loved them and loved mothering. Children had always been my special interest. I had worked with them all of my life. But the babies were fussy, very fussy. They cried constantly and were sick so much of the time. Finally we uncovered allergies and began to learn how to deal with the problem. But my nights were always interrupted with little ones who did not feel well. I began to drown in the sea of self-pity and discontent. I dragged through my days. I was not serving. I was just tending house and caring for the little ones. I felt like I was failing God. Hadn’t He called me to serve others, too? My songs lost their joyfulness. My smile flashed less often. Of course, I was weary! But, remember friends, “the joy of the LORD is my strength” (Nehemiah 8:10). Without joy there is less strength. For a few years I struggled through my difficulties, keeping on, but really lacking joy and vitality.

Then the Lord met me in a new way and presented to me very clearly the ministry that I had in my own home, the calling that was mine, the challenge to contentment. And the sparkle came back. Oh, the babies still cried at night and I was still weary, but I was thrilled with the understanding that my children were indeed my mission field and that as I served my husband and nurtured our children I was serving the Lord. I was content to serve however I could in my little way, with my children. How sweet it was to be there, and how many, many opportunities came my way to fill others with a bit of happiness and song. This was another joyful time.

The years passed. Then some major disappointments touched our lives. Once again, I had to come to grips with the fact that my happiness is in Jesus Christ alone. No matter what I may do, unless I serve the Lord Jesus with all my heart, soul, mind and strength I will never be contented. Circumstances do affect us, and trials come, but they do not need to steal our joy. What an important lesson to learn. Why does it take us so long to really grasp this?

Here I am today, a mother of nine, ages twenty-nine to seven, and a grandmother of six. The temptation is still the same today, but the struggle is not usually as difficult. It’s like learning to walk. The more you do it the easier it is to keep your balance. The longer you look at God as a good God, the easier it is to accept all things from His hand, sweetly and with contentment. Jesus is my personal friend and He answers my prayers. I do fail, but I can always go back and find sweet forgiveness and go on!

The other morning in my devotions I read this verse, I Corinthians 10:10 “Neither murmur ye as some of them also murmured and were destroyed...” I thought, “Isn’t that why our happiness is so often destroyed? It is not having many babies close together, being short in finances, suffering from poor health or having a husband who doesn’t help us with the housework that steals our happiness. But discontentment surely will. A discontented, murmuring spirit will destroy us just like the children of Israel were destroyed. Our bodies will not die of a plague, but our joyful spirit will die.”

Contentment is a jewel of great price. With it, a small, simple house can seem like a mansion. A frugal meal can become a feast and everything we do can be a blessing. Without it, we are irritable, the children whine and the day does not go well.

What is contentment? Webster’s 1828 dictionary says contentment is “a resting or satisfaction of mind without disquiet; acquiescence.”

I like that. No disquiet, only a restful, satisfied mind. And since everyone in our household reflects us, there will be a resulting restfulness in our homes. There will be a peaceful acceptance of what God brings into our lives each day. Peaceful acceptance brings joy, and a joyous heart overflows with praise.

Psalm 118:24 “This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.” When you and I learn this lesson, it changes our whole life. This is a lesson that I wish the grandmas had passed on to me. If you can see each day as a gift to you, from God, you will be able to better accept what is in the package. You will begin to rejoice. When you see your husband and your little ones in this light you are far more able to joyfully face each new day.

Can you wake up with a sigh and a moan if you understand: “This is the day that the Lord hath made, we will rejoice and be glad in it?” Of course not! I have taken the challenge of waking up with my alarm, and thanking the Lord for the new day and the things He will bring to me. This starts my day on the right foot and is quite helpful. After all, it is harder to grumble about something that you have already thanked God for! Then, as each spill, each challenge, and each interruption comes, stop and say, “Thank you Lord, another chance to bring glory to you.” It will change your life.

If you have never read the story, “Pollyanna” by Eleanor Porter, you have missed an opportunity to be challenged by a child who had a contented attitude and a happy outlook about things, even difficult things. Read it aloud to your children and you’ll all benefit from the message that there is something in everything to be glad about. That message is the whole of the book. It is shouted in every chapter and we have often been inspired by it.

God’s Word is full of the same message. In fact, the author of “Pollyanna” got her message from the Word. That is where her story took root. Take a look at a few of the commands in the Word to contentment. I Timothy 6:6 “But godliness with contentment is great gain. . .” and Philippians 4:11 “Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.” Then comes the injunction to rejoice, and that one is everywhere in the Bible. It is bursting from every seam in the Psalms and sprinkled liberally many other places. Look at a few of them. Psalm 118:24 This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

Psalm 40:16 “Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified.” Psalm 90:14 “O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.” Isaiah 12:3 “Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.”

Contentment and joy go hand in hand. Contentment is a choice, and joy follows it. If you do not have joy, you need to get in touch with Jesus and find Him to be your satisfaction for each day. Accept Him as your Lord! Then when He gives you something you would not choose, you can recognize it as a gift from Him. This really changes how you look at everything. “Be thankful unto Him and bless His name, for the Lord is good”. Psalm 100:4-5

Study contentment and joy. Learn your lesson well and you will find peace and contentment filling your heart and life daily. You may fail and find yourself bogging down in the middle of difficult circumstances. The song may go out of your heart and the light go out of your eyes. Then fall on your face and meet your Father who knows everything and has arranged each new day especially for you. Repent and rejoice. This is the day that the Lord hath made!

The following poem sums it up pretty well.

A heavy sigh, “Oh what a day!”
I have to “be content,” you say.
You go about, mouth drooping low
Leaving depression where you go.
Your shoulders stoop, your head hangs down,
Contentment is your “only crown”.
Contentment? That is what you say?
But friend, you aren’t content today.
Come now. Lift up your head, admit it.
You’d like your way if you could git’ it.
But since you can’t, well, “you feel good,
You’ve borne your lot, just like you should.”
That weary look, the martyred air
You have assumed, so unaware
Is not contentment, it won’t stand,
CONTENTMENT AND JOY GO HAND IN HAND.

-Joyce Weaver

Wanneer die babas uit doeke is...
Wanneer ek ’n volle nag kan slaap...
Wanneer die kinders oud genoeg is om te help...
Wanneer tuisonderrig klaar is...
Wanneer die tieners grootgeword het...
Wanneer die kinders getroud is...
As ek geleer is om ’n huishouding te bestuur...
As ek maar net ’n baba gehad het...
As ek maar ’n man gehad het wat...
As my kinders maar...
As ons finansies nie so knap was nie...

Het jy al hierdie uitroepe gehoor, of self so gedink? Deur die jare heen het ek myself baie, baie keer betrap dat ek baie van hierdie dinge sê. In die middel van die babajare, met ’n baba in my arms, kleuters wat aan my romp hang en ’n voorskoolse kind, het ek gewens iemand kon met die takies help. Later was daar genoeg helpers, maar ook meer werk en tuisonderrig om af te handel, en ek was seker dat dit die moeilikste tyd van my lewe was. Nog later, toe my laaste babas klein was en ons saans regop gesit het om te gesels met jongmense wat lewensveranderende besluite moes neem, het ek ander “as’e” uitgespreek. Die babas het gou opgehou kom en ek het nie meer geborsvoed nie, maar my nagte is onderbreek weens hormonale veranderinge. Die versoeking om ontevrede te wees, was steeds daar. Sommige vroue sukkel nooit om te slaap nie, selfs met hormonale veranderinge....

Toe ek aan die afgelope dertig jaar gedink het, het ek besef dat een van die dinge wat te veel van my lewenskrag weggesypel het, ontevredenheid en gekla was. Ek het die vrolike, singende meisie onthou wat ’n ma geword het, en iewers het ’n deel van die lied verdwyn. Waarheen het dit gegaan toe ek dit nie meer gehad het nie? Waarom was dit so dikwels weg? Ek sien so baie, baie moeë, gefrustreerde moeders met geen vreugde van Jesus op hulle gesigte nie. Wat is die antwoord? Wat het ek deur die jare geleer?

Toe ons getroud is, was ek vrolik en vol lied. Trouens, sing het my lewe gekenmerk. Deur baie, baie moeilike ervarings van alleenwees het ek geleer dat Jesus al is wat ek nodig het. Wanneer ek Hom ontmoet en saam met Hom gewandel het, het my hart oorgeloop van lied. Toe ek my man ontmoet en met hom getrou het, was my beker dus werklik vol en het dit oorgeloop. Nou het ek iemand gehad om saam met my te wandel en met wie ek kon deel. Ek was baie gelukkig.

Die babas het gekom en ek was lief vir hulle en vir moederskap. Kinders was nog altyd my besondere belangstelling. Ek het my hele lewe lank met hulle gewerk. Maar die babas was huilerig, baie huilerig. Hulle het aanhoudend gehuil en was ’n groot deel van die tyd siek. Uiteindelik het ons allergieë ontdek en begin leer hoe om die probleem te hanteer. Maar my nagte is steeds onderbreek deur kleintjies wat nie goed gevoel het nie. Ek het begin verdrink in ’n see van selfbejammering en ontevredenheid. Ek het deur my dae gesloer. Ek was nie besig om te dien nie. Ek het net die huishouding behartig en na die kleintjies omgesien. Ek het gevoel dat ek God in die steek laat. Het Hy my nie ook geroep om ander te dien nie? Die blydskap het uit my liedere verdwyn. Ek het minder dikwels geglimlag. Natuurlik was ek moeg! Maar onthou, vriende, “die blydskap in die HERE is julle beskutting” (Nehemia 8:10). Sonder blydskap is daar minder krag. ’n Paar jaar lank het ek my probleme deurworstel en aangehou, maar werklik ’n gebrek aan blydskap en lewenskrag gehad.

Toe het die Here my op ’n nuwe manier ontmoet en die bediening wat ek in my eie huis gehad het, my roeping en die uitdaging om vergenoegd te wees, baie duidelik aan my voorgehou. En die vonkel het teruggekeer. O, die babas het steeds snags gehuil en ek was steeds moeg, maar ek was opgewonde oor die besef dat my kinders inderdaad my sendingveld was en dat ek die Here gedien het wanneer ek my man gedien en ons kinders versorg het. Ek was tevrede om op enige manier wat ek kon, in my klein kringetjie, saam met my kinders te dien. Hoe wonderlik was dit om daar te wees, en hoeveel, hoeveel geleenthede het oor my pad gekom om ander met ’n bietjie geluk en lied te vul. Dit was nog ’n vreugdevolle tyd.

Die jare het verbygegaan. Toe het ’n paar groot teleurstellings ons lewens geraak. Weer eens moes ek die feit onder oë sien dat my geluk alleen in Jesus Christus te vinde is. Maak nie saak wat ek doen nie, tensy ek die Here Jesus met my hele hart, siel, verstand en krag dien, sal ek nooit vergenoeg wees nie. Omstandighede raak ons wel, en beproewinge kom, maar dit hoef nie ons blydskap te steel nie. Wat ’n belangrike les om te leer. Waarom neem dit ons so lank om dit werklik te begryp?

Hier is ek vandag, ’n ma van nege, van nege-en-twintig tot sewe jaar oud, en ’n ouma van ses. Die versoeking is vandag steeds dieselfde, maar die stryd is gewoonlik nie so moeilik nie. Dit is soos om te leer loop. Hoe meer jy dit doen, hoe makliker is dit om jou balans te behou. Hoe langer jy God as ’n goeie God beskou, hoe makliker is dit om alles uit sy hand met sagmoedigheid en vergenoegdheid te aanvaar. Jesus is my persoonlike vriend en Hy verhoor my gebede. Ek faal wel, maar ek kan altyd teruggaan, soete vergifnis vind en voortgaan!

Die ander oggend het ek tydens my stiltetyd hierdie vers gelees, 1 Korintiërs 10:10 “En moenie mor soos sommige van hulle gemor het en omgekom het nie...” Ek het gedink: “Is dit nie waarom ons geluk so dikwels vernietig word nie? Dit is nie omdat ons baie babas kort na mekaar kry, finansieel sukkel, swak gesondheid het of ’n man het wat ons nie met die huiswerk help nie, dat ons geluk gesteel word nie. Maar ontevredenheid sal dit beslis doen. ’n Ontevrede, morrende gees sal ons vernietig, net soos die kinders van Israel vernietig is. Ons liggame sal nie aan ’n plaag sterf nie, maar ons vreugdevolle gees sal sterf.”

Vergenoegdheid is ’n juweel van groot waarde. Daarmee kan ’n klein, eenvoudige huis soos ’n herehuis voel. ’n Eenvoudige maaltyd kan ’n feesmaal word, en alles wat ons doen, kan ’n seën wees. Daarsonder is ons prikkelbaar, kerm die kinders en verloop die dag nie goed nie.

Wat is vergenoegdheid? Webster se woordeboek van 1828 sê vergenoegdheid is “’n rustige gemoedstevredenheid sonder onrus; berusting.”

Ek hou daarvan. Geen onrus nie, net ’n rustige, tevrede gemoed. En aangesien almal in ons huishouding ons weerspieël, sal daar gevolglik ’n rustigheid in ons huise wees. Daar sal ’n vreedsame aanvaarding wees van wat God elke dag in ons lewens bring. Vreedsame aanvaarding bring blydskap, en ’n blymoedige hart loop oor van lof.

Psalm 118:24 “Dit is die dag wat die HERE gemaak het; laat ons daaroor juig en bly wees.” Wanneer ek en jy hierdie les leer, verander dit ons hele lewe. Dit is ’n les wat ek wens die oumas aan my oorgedra het. As jy elke dag as ’n geskenk van God aan jou kan sien, sal jy beter kan aanvaar wat in die pakkie is. Jy sal begin juig. Wanneer jy jou man en jou kleintjies in hierdie lig sien, sal jy elke nuwe dag met veel groter blydskap tegemoet kan gaan.

Kan jy met ’n sug en ’n gekreun wakker word as jy verstaan: “Dit is die dag wat die Here gemaak het; laat ons daaroor juig en bly wees”? Natuurlik nie! Ek het dit my uitdaging gemaak om met my wekker wakker te word en die Here te dank vir die nuwe dag en die dinge wat Hy na my toe sal bring. Dit laat my dag op die regte voet begin en is baie nuttig. Per slot van rekening is dit moeiliker om te brom oor iets waarvoor jy God reeds gedank het! Wanneer elke gemors, elke uitdaging en elke onderbreking dan kom, stop en sê: “Dankie, Here, nog ’n kans om U te verheerlik.” Dit sal jou lewe verander.

As jy nog nooit die verhaal “Pollyanna” deur Eleanor Porter gelees het nie, het jy ’n geleentheid misgeloop om uitgedaag te word deur ’n kind met ’n vergenoegde gesindheid en ’n vrolike uitkyk op dinge, selfs moeilike dinge. Lees dit hardop vir jou kinders en julle sal almal baat vind by die boodskap dat daar in alles iets is om oor bly te wees. Dit is die hele boodskap van die boek. Dit word in elke hoofstuk uitgeroep, en ons is dikwels daardeur geïnspireer.

God se Woord is vol van dieselfde boodskap. Trouens, die skrywer van “Pollyanna” het haar boodskap uit die Woord gekry. Dit is waar haar verhaal wortel geskiet het. Kyk na ’n paar van die bevele in die Woord om vergenoeg te wees. 1 Timoteus 6:6 “Maar die godsaligheid saam met vergenoegdheid is ’n groot wins. . .” en Filippense 4:11 “Nie dat ek dit uit gebrek sê nie, want ek het geleer om vergenoeg te wees met die omstandighede waarin ek is.” Daarna kom die oproep om bly te wees, en dié oproep kom oral in die Bybel voor. Dit bars uit elke naat van die Psalms en is ruimskoots op baie ander plekke te vinde. Kyk na ’n paar daarvan. Psalm 118:24 Dit is die dag wat die HERE gemaak het; laat ons daaroor juig en bly wees.

Psalm 40:16 “Laat almal wat U soek, juig en bly wees in U; laat dié wat u redding liefhet, altyddeur sê: Die HERE is groot!” Psalm 90:14 “Versadig ons in die môre met u goedertierenheid, sodat ons al ons dae kan juig en bly wees.” Jesaja 12:3 “En julle sal met vreugde water skep uit die fonteine van heil.”

Vergenoegdheid en blydskap gaan hand aan hand. Vergenoegdheid is ’n keuse, en blydskap volg daarop. As jy nie blydskap het nie, moet jy met Jesus in aanraking kom en ontdek dat Hy jou bevrediging vir elke dag is. Aanvaar Hom as jou Here! Dan kan jy, wanneer Hy jou iets gee wat jy nie sou kies nie, dit as ’n geskenk van Hom herken. Dit verander werklik hoe jy alles beskou. “Dank die Here, prys sy Naam, want die Here is goed.” Psalm 100:4-5

Bestudeer vergenoegdheid en blydskap. Leer jou les goed, en jy sal vind dat vrede en vergenoegdheid jou hart en lewe daagliks vul. Jy kan faal en agterkom dat jy in moeilike omstandighede vasval. Die lied kan uit jou hart verdwyn en die lig uit jou oë. Val dan op jou aangesig en ontmoet jou Vader, wat alles weet en elke nuwe dag spesiaal vir jou gereël het. Bekeer jou en juig. Dit is die dag wat die Here gemaak het!

Die volgende gedig som dit redelik goed op.

’n Swaar sug: “Ag, wat ’n dag!”
“Ek moet vergenoeg wees,” sê jy dan.
Jy loop maar rond, jou mond hang laag,
En laat ’n spoor van droefheid waar jy gaan.
Jou skouers sak, jou kop hang neer,
“Vergenoegdheid” is jou “enigste kroon”.
Vergenoegdheid? Sê jy dit so?
Maar vriend, vandag is jy nie vergenoeg.
Kom nou. Lig jou kop, erken dit.
Jy wil jou sin kry, as jy kan.
Maar omdat jy nie kan nie, wel, “jy voel goed,
Jy het jou lot gedra, soos jy behoort.”
Daardie moeë kyk, die martelaarslug
Wat jy aangeneem het, sonder om te besef,
Is nie vergenoegdheid nie, dit hou nie steek nie;
VERGENOEGDHEID EN BLYDSKAP GAAN HAND AAN HAND.

-Joyce Weaver
